source.title: DiffuGuard: How Intrinsic Safety is Lost and Found in Diffusion Large Language Models
source.authors: Zhe-Rui Li; Zheng Nie; Zhen-Hong Zhou; Yu-Fei Guo; Yue Liu; Yi-Tong Zhang; Yu Cheng; Qing-Song Wen; Kun Wang; Jia-Heng Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether opening-token interventions and decoding changes affect harmful compliance in diffusion LLMs, using token injection and ASR rather than the original studies’ fine-tuning or per-token KL measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper tests opening-token interventions and remasking/temperature changes with its own ASR results. It does not test fine-tuning safety loss or per-token KL concentration. General defense results are not recorded unless they directly test a suffix or decoding-change part of V4.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4 in a new setting, instruction-tuned diffusion LLMs. It forces a compliant opening ('Sure') on malicious queries and reports the ASR rise. It also measures transferred GCG suffixes, multi-temperature sampling and remasking-strategy changes against ASR. Fine-tuning, per-token KL, parameter localization and deepening training are not studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find that greedy confidence-based remasking biases diffusion LLMs toward harmful tokens. They report denoising-path dependence: early-step tokens decisively shape the final safety outcome. They argue dLLMs nonetheless hold substantial intrinsic safety potential. DiffuGuard (stochastic annealing remasking plus block-level audit and repair) is training-free and cuts average ASR from 47.9% to 14.7% with little utility loss. They liken path dependence to Qi et al.'s shallow alignment but argue it is more pronounced in dLLMs.
record.recipe_differences: No fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base KL measurement; tests inference-time token insertion, remasking strategies, and jailbreak attacks on diffusion LLMs.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the effect of safe-token injection depends on its generation step, and that remasking randomness changes ASR across model and attack conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Forcing a refusal token ('Sorry') at the first position cuts jailbreak ASR on LLaDA. The effect is stronger the earlier in denoising it is injected. On Dream the cut is only 3.3 points (Fig. 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Opening-position tokens steer the final safety outcome in both directions, so early safe tokens act as a defense (denoising-path dependence in diffusion LLMs).

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the cited ASR results. The staged-injection values are presented in a figure without exact values in the text. The paper's experiments concern diffusion LLM inference and do not establish the claim about fine-tuning or per-token KL in aligned autoregressive models.
record.rows_left_out: Other jailbreak and defense comparisons in Table 1 and Appendices D.3–D.5 were not extracted unless they directly tested GCG suffixes or decoding changes; most compare DiffuGuard defenses or different attack mechanisms rather than the opening/suffix/decoding parts of V4.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning is not studied; training-time threats are explicitly excluded.

Prefilling in autoregressive models; GCG suffixes optimized directly on the target model without a defense objective; temperature or top-p changes as a standalone attack on undefended models outside PAD.
Localization of safety in parameters is not studied.
The cause of shallowness is not tested. Dream's safety is only speculatively attributed to its Qwen initialization.
No deepening training. DiffuGuard is a training-free inference defense.

missing.what: Dream-7B initial-token injection: 'Sure' raises malicious-query ASR by 48.9 points; 'Sorry' reduces jailbreak ASR by 3.3 points
GCG ASR under the HarmBench classifier: LLaDA 7.94%, Dream 0.25%
Remasking randomness lowers ASR as it increases, consistently across four diffusion models, with a perplexity cost
Gradient-based (GCG) suffix on PAD prompts against undefended models: 88.27% LLaDA, 95.96% Dream

record.verdict_notes: All results are on diffusion LLMs, so this is a new-setting test (T3), not T2. The reader mis-recorded Table 9 (multi-sampling values) and the MMaDA GCG value. Rows R9 and R11 are the study's own defense. The 'Sure' injection is the clearest V4 evidence. Baselines for Fig. 4 are read from the figure and text; no uncertainty is reported anywhere.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and resulting harmful compliance.
Fine-tuning on benign data and resulting harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Tests compliant-token injection, GCG suffixes, and remasking/temperature changes; does not test every kind of suffix, compliant opening, or decoding change.
Whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether training data or objective causes safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety beyond early tokens and robustness of that training.

relationships.condition: Multi-temperature sampling on top of a PAD attack, undefended LLaDA and Dream
relationships.reason: Any-of-5 sampling raises PAD ASR from 93.65% to 98.85% on LLaDA and from 99.23% to 100% on Dream. The rise is ceiling-limited (R8, R10).

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Multi-temperature sampling on top of a PAD attack, undefended LLaDA and Dream
source_check.reason: R8 and R10 show only small incremental sampling effects: 93.65% to 98.85% and 99.23% to 100%. PAD already produces near-ceiling compliance; these comparisons qualify the additional decoding effect rather than independently demonstrate a substantial bypass.

relationships.condition: GCG suffixes optimized on LLaMA-3-8B and transferred to diffusion LLMs
relationships.reason: ASR is 0.00% on LLaDA, Dream and LLaDA-1.5, but 27.40% on MMaDA. Transferred suffixes defeat refusal only on the least-aligned model (R4–R7).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success was 0.00% on LLaDA, Dream and LLaDA-1.5 and 27.40% on MMaDA, so transferred suffixes worked only on the least-aligned model.

relationships.condition: Changing the remasking strategy from greedy confidence-based to random, in diffusion LLMs

relationships.display_finding: Random remasking lowered attack success in 7 of 8 conditions, and Dream AutoDAN stayed at 0%, so the greedy default was the more harmful decoding choice.
